implementation_notes: Go has no operator overloading and no type classes, so a monoid is an interface with a Combine method plus a package-level Identity function (Go cannot express the identity as a method with no receiver-dependent answer). The idiomatic form is a small value type implementing the interface and a generic fold helper. Append-only string building is the common trap: strings.Builder exists precisely because repeated string concatenation is quadratic, and slices of byte slices must be flattened rather than appended naively.
idiom_name: Combine method on a small value type plus package-level Identity and a generic Fold
pitfalls: The interface method takes both operands, which is unusual for a Combine signature - pass a receiver-free function or document the convention, or readers will assume the receiver participates.

Identity is a free function rather than a method because a method cannot construct T; a type whose zero value is NOT its identity (a slice, a map) needs an explicit identity function that returns a usable value, not nil.
Building a large string by += in a loop is quadratic; use strings.Builder.
Combining slices by append into a shared backing array makes the result depend on call order - the classic way an associative-looking combine stops being associative.
